quests.instruction: Ravi does not know what a word in the story means, so he puts up his hand to find out. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: He wants to find out something he does not know.
quests.explanation: Ask means to put a question to someone because you want to know something.
quests.funFact: A good question can be even more useful than a quick answer.

quests.instruction: The teacher says, 'What is five plus three?' and Sara says, 'Eight.' What does Sara do?
quests.hint: She gives the information the teacher wanted.
quests.explanation: Answer means to say or write something back when someone asks you a question.
quests.funFact: A question usually ends with a question mark, but an answer often ends with a full stop.

quests.instruction: In class, you should ___ your hand if you want to speak.
quests.hint: Your hand goes up, not down.
quests.explanation: Raise means to lift something up to a higher place.
quests.funFact: Raise also means to bring up children, plants or animals.

quests.instruction: Mia says the letters of 'cat' one by one: C, A, T. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: Each letter is said in the right order.
quests.explanation: Spell means to say or write the letters of a word in the right order.
quests.funFact: English has some tricky spellings, like 'knight', where the k is silent.

quests.instruction: Ben puts thin paper over a drawing and follows the lines with his pencil. What does he do?
quests.hint: The original picture shows through the paper.
quests.explanation: Trace means to follow the lines of a shape with a pencil, often over a picture.
quests.funFact: Tracing letters helps young children learn to write them.

quests.instruction: Noor looks at the board and writes the same words in her notebook. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: She makes her own version of what she sees.
quests.explanation: Copy means to make something the same as something else, such as writing the same words.
quests.funFact: Before printing, people made copies of books by writing them out by hand.

quests.instruction: Leo wrote the wrong number, so he rubs it away with a rubber. What is he doing?
quests.hint: His pencil mark disappears.
quests.explanation: Erase means to remove writing or marks so that they cannot be seen.
quests.funFact: Early rubbers were not rubber at all: people once used bread to rub out pencil.

quests.instruction: To show the most important word, Zoe draws a line beneath it. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: The line goes below the word.
quests.explanation: Underline means to draw a line under a word so it stands out.
quests.funFact: Some books use bold or slanted letters instead of underlining.

quests.instruction: The teacher asks the children to put a ring around the correct answer. What should they do?
quests.hint: Their pencils draw a round shape.
quests.explanation: Circle means to draw a ring around something to show it. 'Circle' is also the name of the shape.
quests.funFact: A circle has no corners, and every point on it is the same distance from the centre.

quests.instruction: Tom lays a ruler along his pencil to find out how long it is. What is he doing?
quests.hint: Numbers on the ruler tell him the answer.
quests.explanation: Measure means to find out the size, length or amount of something.
quests.funFact: The metre was first defined by scientists in France over two hundred years ago.

quests.instruction: Priya has three apples and gets two more. She puts them together to find the total. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: The number gets bigger.
quests.explanation: Add means to put numbers or things together to get a bigger total.
quests.funFact: The plus sign (+) is the picture of 'add' used all over the world.

quests.instruction: Dev has nine stickers and gives four away. To find how many are left, he must ___.
quests.hint: The number gets smaller.
quests.explanation: Subtract means to take one number away from another.
quests.funFact: Subtraction is the opposite of addition.

quests.instruction: Aisha has a big bag of grapes and gives some to each of her friends. What is she doing?
quests.hint: Everyone gets a part.
quests.explanation: Share means to give a part of something to others or to use it together.
quests.funFact: Many playgrounds work well only when children share the swings.

quests.instruction: At the water fountain, the children stand one behind another in a straight row. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: Everyone stands one behind the other.
quests.explanation: Line up means to stand in a row, one behind the other, usually to wait.
quests.funFact: In British English, a line of people waiting is called a queue.

quests.instruction: The slide is busy, so Max stays quietly in place until it is his turn. What is he doing?
quests.hint: Nothing happens until his turn comes.
quests.explanation: Wait means to stay in one place until something happens or someone comes.
quests.funFact: 'Wait' and 'weight' sound exactly the same but mean different things.

quests.instruction: Mrs Rao goes from desk to desk and takes everyone's homework notebook. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: She gathers many things into one place.
quests.explanation: Collect means to bring things together from different places or people.
quests.funFact: Some people collect stamps, shells or coins as a hobby.

quests.instruction: Before the art lesson, the teacher gives one sheet of paper to every child. What does she do?
quests.hint: One thing goes to each person.
quests.explanation: Hand out means to give something to each person in a group.
quests.funFact: 'Handout' can also be a noun: a sheet that a teacher gives to the class.

quests.instruction: Rina borrowed a pencil from her friend, and now she gives it back. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: The pencil goes back to its owner.
quests.explanation: Return means to give something back or go back to a place.
quests.funFact: Library books are returned by a certain date so that other people can read them.

quests.instruction: Kofi puts his books on top of one another in a neat pile. What does he do?
quests.hint: A pile grows upward.
quests.explanation: Stack means to put things on top of each other in a pile.
quests.funFact: A stack of paper is called a ream when it has 500 sheets.

quests.instruction: Hana puts all the red crayons in one box and all the blue crayons in another. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: Things that belong together go together.
quests.explanation: Sort means to put things into groups of the same kind.
quests.funFact: Post offices sort letters by place so they reach the right house.

quests.instruction: When the lesson ends, the children return the scissors to their cupboard. What do they do?
quests.hint: The scissors go back where they belong.
quests.explanation: Put away means to return something to its proper place after you have used it.
quests.funFact: Tidying up after yourself is a habit that saves time later.

quests.instruction: Anu gets flour, sugar and eggs and prepares a cake. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: Ingredients are turned into something new.
quests.explanation: Make means to create or prepare something by putting things together.
quests.funFact: 'Make' is one of the most-used verbs in English.

quests.instruction: Raj needs to cut paper, so he picks up the scissors and does the job with them. What does he do?
quests.hint: The scissors are a tool that helps him.
quests.explanation: Use means to take something and do a job with it.
quests.funFact: The word 'use' sounds different as a noun, as in 'What is the use of this?'

quests.instruction: Mum says, '___ your bag on the hook, please.'
quests.hint: The bag moves to a place and stays there.
quests.explanation: Put means to place something somewhere.
quests.funFact: 'Put' keeps the same form in the past: yesterday I put my bag on the hook.

quests.instruction: A pan has food stuck on it, so Dad rubs it hard with a brush. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: Gentle rubbing will not be enough.
quests.explanation: Scrub means to rub something hard to get it very clean.
quests.funFact: Scrub is also the name for small bushes that grow in dry land.

quests.instruction: Thin grey powder covers the shelf, so Nina wipes it off with a soft cloth. What is she doing?
quests.hint: The dirt is as light as powder.
quests.explanation: Dust means to clean dust from furniture and surfaces. Dust is also the name of the powder itself.
quests.funFact: House dust is made of tiny pieces of skin, hair and fibres from clothes.

quests.instruction: The floor is covered with sticky footprints. Dad uses a bucket of soapy water and a long handle with a cloth head. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: He cleans the floor using water.
quests.explanation: Mop means to clean a floor with a wet mop. Sweep is with a dry broom.
quests.funFact: A mop holds much more water than a cloth does, so it covers a floor faster.

quests.instruction: Mum writes 'Flour' on the jar so everyone knows what is inside. What does she do?
quests.hint: A name goes on the jar.
quests.explanation: Label means to put a name or information on something.
quests.funFact: Food labels tell you what is in the food and how to keep it fresh.

quests.instruction: Ella presses the lid down firmly on her lunch box so nothing can leak out. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: The box has to close tightly.
quests.explanation: Seal means to close something tightly so that nothing gets in or out.
quests.funFact: Some sealed bags let air out but not in, which keeps food fresh for longer.

quests.instruction: For her friend's birthday, Meena covers the present in coloured paper. What does she do?
quests.hint: Paper goes around the whole present.
quests.explanation: Wrap means to cover something by putting paper or cloth around it.
quests.funFact: In Japan, wrapping with cloth is an art called furoshiki.
